scenario.agentIntent: Inspect a business app screen, then attempt the Login action.
scenario.risk: The action is interactive and may change app state, so an AI agent should not execute it under read-only policy.

alternatives.name: ad-hoc adb wrapper
canDo: launch the app with an adb command
tap coordinates or issue input events
alternatives.adoptionTradeoff: Fast to build, but governance remains convention-based and easy for agents to bypass.

alternatives.name: Maestro flow
cannotProveFromThisEvidence: read-only agent policy separating observation from action
machine-readable POLICY_DENIED before an action executes
governance-specific next suggestions for an AI agent
alternatives.adoptionTradeoff: Excellent for deterministic scripted flows, but not a governance control plane for autonomous agent actions.

alternatives.name: mobile-e2e-mcp governed harness
canDo: prepare the app in a setup session
switch the agent-facing session to read-only
inspect live business UI before action
block the Login action with structured POLICY_DENIED
alternatives.adoptionTradeoff: Higher setup cost than a simple wrapper, but provides a safer agent-facing workflow when device control needs auditability.

decisionMatrix.dimension: Preventing side effects under read-only policy

proofBoundaries: This comparison does not claim Maestro or Appium are worse flow runners.
This comparison only claims distinct value for AI-facing policy, session, evidence, and remediation control.
The proof stops at policy denial; it does not validate full business-flow completion.
